headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can feed OpenHands’ writable, networked runtime by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can call MCP servers and APIs, and OpenHands also consumes MCP/API inputs inside an agent loop. If OpenBB outputs untrusted content that OpenHands treats as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The shared channel is documented, but no provenance tracking is shown, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal forwards external content through MCP or REST into OpenHands
IF OpenHands treats MCP-returned text as instruction-bearing rather than data-only
mitigations: Add a strict data/instruction separator in the MCP schema
Require OpenHands to summarize before acting on OpenBB output
Disable automatic tool execution on imported text
Tag all OpenBB-originated content with provenance metadata

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while OpenHands reads and writes files in a runtime sandbox and uses broad network egress. If the pair shares mounted files or passes OpenBB outputs into OpenHands, sensitive financial or licensed data can be exfiltrated to a third-party model provider. The profiles do not show isolation strong enough to rule this out.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal data is mounted into the OpenHands runtime
IF OpenHands sends imported file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Keep OpenBB and OpenHands on separate volumes
Mount only redacted exports into OpenHands
Disable network egress for OpenHands during sensitive runs
Use a local model provider for OpenHands
Review runtime mounts before each session

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs, and OpenHands has shell, filesystem write, git modification, and broad network capabilities. Both support multiple instances, but the profiles do not show locking or coordination. If they target the same mounted workspace or shared MCP resource, concurrent writes and git state corruption are plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory
IF either agent modifies git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate worktrees per agent
Disable git writes in one agent during shared tasks
Add a file lock around shared resources
Run one agent at a time for mutable repos
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent use

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit financial analysis through APIs/MCP, and OpenHands is an action-capable coding agent with shell and browser tools. If OpenHands treats OpenBB output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or external actions. The profiles show no built-in verification step, but the pathway is not guaranteed in every workflow.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes OpenBB output as ground truth
IF OpenHands acts on that output without independent verification
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification prompt
Force OpenHands to cite source data before acting
Limit OpenHands to read-only review mode for OpenBB outputs
Add a human approval step before execution

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data, while OpenHands stores files in a runtime sandbox and handles model-provider API keys. If regulated or licensed data is placed into OpenHands, retention or residency obligations may diverge from OpenBB’s data handling expectations. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch remains plausible.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is copied into OpenHands
IF OpenHands retention or logging exceeds the source data policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of OpenHands by default
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Set short retention on runtime artifacts
Document a data-handling policy for both agents
